column1: # The host-path table of `just affected --narrow` (tools/recipes.py, the section above narrow()).
# glob<TAB>recipes<TAB>why. A changed file that some gate reads through a dependency edge (a lib a target links,
# a manifest, a cargo global) selects the recipes of every row whose glob matches it; `*` keeps the full list; no
# row keeps the full list and names the file. A file's own target (its bin, its test file, its lib's own tests), a
# script a recipe names, and the recipe's own text select their recipes without a row, so a row names only the gates
# that reach the file through a dependency; gate-ptx-spill joins a narrowed list only when a scan pair is not identical
# or its own inputs moved (tools/recipes.py, narrow()). `**` crosses `/`, `*` does not,
# `{a,b}` is either. `just check-recipes` holds each row to the tree: its recipes are gate recipes that link every file
# it matches, each alternative matches a file, and every gate whose own target names the module the glob stands for
# is in the row. The recipe lists came from the module references of each gate's targets, read transitively through
# the workspace libs (use trees and paths, not docs); where the why names a run-time dispatch, the static reference
# alone would have named more gates.
# Every binary parses the registry and runs at_main first, and a lever's default reaches whoever reads it in place.
